date_note: Publication day of the Egovernment article; it does not state the date of the Bundesrat vote. The Bundestag adopted the bill on 12 November 2026.
exec: German security authorities gain active cyber-defence powers, per Egovernment, which could touch systems and traffic.
plain: Germany's upper house is reported to have approved a law giving the BSI, federal police and BKA powers to act against cyberattacks, not only to prevent them.
summary: Egovernment reports that the Bundesrat approved a law giving the BSI, the federal police and the BKA powers for active cyber defence, after the Bundestag adopted the government's bill on 12 November 2026. The powers include prohibiting the operation of dangerous IT systems, redirecting harmful data traffic, and reading, deleting or altering data. The Länder had asked for changes, which the government largely rejected, the article says.
title: Germany's Bundesrat reportedly approves active cyber-defence powers for BSI, BKA and federal police

validation.note: Single publisher: Egovernment; Healthcare Digital carries the same article (same id), so it is not independent. Bundesrat's own page not read.
